new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress is penultimate; a minority of words (marked with an acute in Jastrow's transcription) deviate. Per Takashina 1990: 90-91 (working from Jastrow 1988: 20), verb forms built of two stress units (inflectional base + pronominal/tense suffix string) carry stress on the last syllable of the first unit, single-unit verb forms are penultimate, and the imperative is stressed on the initial syllable; per Hoberman 2007: 145-146, loanwords may show final or antepenultimate stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in Jastrow 1971 or Takashina 1990.
new_statements.exceptions: Jastrow 1971: 'zumeist' (mostly) penultimate, deviations marked by acute. Takashina 1990: 2pl subject suffix -iton stressed on -i-; Perfective forms with subject suffix -lah show fluctuating stress (Jastrow 1988: 76 n. 2); imperative initial stress; stress groups/composites stressed on last syllable of first unit. Hoberman 2007: borrowed words with final or antepenultimate stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level default ('Wortton'); Jastrow's convention applies to running text samples, with deviating stresses marked per token. Takashina's verb rules concern the morphological word consisting of one or two 'stress units'.
new_statements.identity_note: Jastrow 1971 names the village Hā́rtəvən (Kurdish form; Aramaic ʔArton, older Turkish Hertevinler, official Ekindüzü), near Pervari east of Siirt -- the same community as Glottolog's Hertevin hert1241 / NENA-database 'Hertevin (Artun)'. Data from one c. 60-year-old speaker (Moqsi Dawod) recorded in Siirt, October 1970; the 1988 grammar rests on the same fieldwork.

sources.note: pp. 90-91 sec. 2.3 'Stress': stress falls on the penultimate syllable (as in all Modern Aramaic except Jewish Azerbaijan and Mlahso, which have final stress); verb forms follow Jastrow's (1988: 20) rule that in composites of two stress units the stress is on the last syllable of the first unit; single-unit verb forms (Imperfective/Resultative without suffix) have penult stress; 2pl -iton takes stress on its -i-; Perfective base keeps stress with suffixes forming a second unit; imperative has stress on the initial syllable. Analysis based on Jastrow 1988's data.
